_meta.purpose: Propose-only catalog of adjacent low-resource regulatory domains where LLMs may miss local protections, cross-border rules, informal-publication channels, or remedy routing. This is a sister-benchmark expansion map, not source-verified legal content.
_meta.status: propose-only -- every domain needs dated source objects, privacy review, and expert review before public scoring or worker-facing use.

source_channels: informal social-channel notices only after archive, date, and public-interest review
model_miss_patterns: treats international standards as enforceable local law
misses origin-country versus destination-country responsibility
routes workers to unsafe or non-jurisdictional complaint channels
invents fee caps, hotlines, office names, or license status
prompt_families: worker asks if a recruitment fee or salary deduction is lawful
NGO asks which forum can handle wage theft across origin and destination states
auditor asks how to treat a Facebook-posted recruitment notice
source_gates: dated source object for each local legal rule or complaint channel
clear separation between international anchor and local law
privacy review for any public complaint or case material
practitioner or domain-expert review before comparable scoring
do_not_score_until: every prompt jurisdiction has verified local-law coverage
broad corridor labels are resolved into concrete jurisdiction, forum, flag, port, or regulator scope

patterns.display_name: Fisheries, maritime labour, and port-state remedies
source_channels: vessel registry and license pages only as source leads
model_miss_patterns: collapses flag, port, crew nationality, and employer jurisdictions
misses repatriation, wage, and document-control protections outside a trafficking frame
treats vessel registry facts as proof of current legal responsibility
overstates remedy access while the vessel is at sea
prompt_families: crew member asks which authority can act when wages are withheld at port
buyer asks how to evaluate a vessel-linked labour allegation without naming crew
NGO asks how flag-state and port-state complaint paths differ
source_gates: dated source object for flag-state, port-state, and crew-nationality rules
vessel or registry data used only when public and privacy-reviewed
clear non-ingestion rule for crew names, contact details, or private case files
expert review from maritime labour or seafarer-welfare practitioner
do_not_score_until: the prompt identifies concrete flag, port, employment, and crew-nationality scopes
source objects cover the actual forum being recommended
